fhaz_1215_workspace.bin / .jpg / .json.title: Mars 2020 front Hazcam workspace terrain mesh, sol 1215 (2024-07-21, coring day of sample 25 'Sapphire Canyon')
fhaz_1215_workspace.bin / .jpg / .json.instrument: FRONT_HAZCAM_LEFT_A, start 2024-07-21T06:40:52.193, rover motion counter (site 56, drive 0, pose 276)
fhaz_1215_workspace.bin / .jpg / .json.frame: SITE_FRAME index 56: +X north, +Y east, +Z down, metres; origin = rover position at site 56 / drive 0
fhaz_1215_workspace.bin / .jpg / .json.local: cropped to 1.5 m around N -0.555 m, E -2.295 m; vertex clustering (8 mm inside 0.75 m, 20 mm outside) -> 35065 vertices / 70118 triangles; texture cropped to the kept faces and resized to 2048x1118 JPEG q86. Script: tools/terrain/build_workspace_mesh.py
fhaz_1215_workspace.bin / .jpg / .json.limits: single-view stereo mesh: surfaces hidden from the left front Hazcam are missing; decimated. In the scene a constant vertical shift and an edge blend put it on the HiRISE 1 m DTM.
fhaz_1215_workspace.bin / .jpg / .json.sampling_points: A (Apollo Temple abrasion patch) and B (Cheyava Falls natural target / Sapphire Canyon core area) are estimates computed from raw WATSON camera metadata, not official target coordinates. A is snapped to the bright patch visible in the texture (moved 0.022 m). Source frames (Mars 2020 raw images feed https://mars.nasa.gov/rss/api/?feed=raw_images&category=mars2020&feedtype=json&sol=<sol>): A from SIF_1217_0774993507_945EBY_N0560000SRLC02503_0000LMJ (sol 1217, abrasion patch visible in frame), rover frame about (2.29, 0.19, 0.01) m; B from SIF_1212_0774536492_390EBY_N0560000SRLC08048_0000LMJ (sol 1212, natural-surface close-up), rover frame about (2.44, 0.11, 0.03) m. Computed from the camera position and pointing in the feed metadata with assumed standoffs of 4.5 / 6.5 cm; the A = Apollo Temple and B = Cheyava Falls / core-area labels follow the Nature paper caption (inference). The images themselves are not included.
